newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan praises Canada's freeing of 6 sailors.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan praises Canada's freeing of 6 sailors.

text.p: Taiwan on Friday welcomed a verdict by a Canadian court that freed six Taiwanese sailors accused of killing three Romanian stowaways.
"We feel affirmative and pleased by the Nova Scotia Supreme Court verdict to free six of our sailors," Taiwan's foreign ministry said in a statement.
It called on Canadian Justice Minister Allan Rock to stand by the ruling and speedily hand over the crew, the ship and other items to Taiwan's judicial authorities to handle the case.
Rock said in a statement that Canadian government prosecutors, acting on behalf of Romania, had appealed the decision.
Supreme Court Judge Michael MacDonald decided to free the six on the grounds that Canada had no jurisdiction to extradite the men to Romania to face murder charges.
He said the alleged crimes occurred on a Taiwan ship in international waters, rather than on a Romanian ship or territory.

But he added that if he had jurisdiction, he would have placed the sailors and all officers of the merchant ship Maersk Dubai on trial on manslaughter and second-degree murder charges for casting the stowaways adrift, which lead to their presumed deaths.
Filipino sailors who jumped ship from the Maersk Dubai to Nova Scotia accused the ship's captain and officers of forcing the stowaways overboard in two separate incidents.
Defense lawyers acknowledged that two stowaways were forced off the ship in March 1996, but said they were given lifejackets, food and water and were in sight of land when cast overboard.
The Filipino sailors said another Romanian stowaway was thrown off the ship in May. The bodies of the three have not been found, and their families have not heard from them.
The case has become an international diplomatic dispute.
Romania has sought the extradition of the six Taiwan sailors, but Taiwan says it has jurisdiction in the case. China, claiming sovereignty over Taiwan, says Beijing should decide the sailors' fate.
